name: Skinwalk Sunday
description: Skinwalk Sunday originated in 2214 in the Shelf's Ward 2 geneware modification community as a single-day public showcase where anyone who had undergone cosmetic or functional geneware modification — bioluminescent skin, fur, tails, horn growth, chromatophore patterning — could walk the streets openly without fear of the social and professional penalties that still existed in upper tiers. The event spread rapidly through Tier 2 and 3 as geneware became more affordable, and now constitutes the largest single gathering of genetically modified individuals in the Great Lakes corridor, held annually on the last Sunday of August.
cultural_impact: Skinwalk Sunday has functionally normalized visible geneware modification in Tiers 1-3 — the annual visibility event has done more to shift public perception of geneware than any corporate marketing campaign, which is why multiple corponations have attempted to co-opt it as a product showcase.
key_figures: Lyra (E.L.F. event coordinator, runs the Skinwalk route logistics)
Councilor Adaeze Petrov-Yamamoto (attempted to legislate the event in 2221, failed)
locations: Ward 2 Origin Block, Shelf — the 'Root Walk' starting point
The Calumet Mile, Tier 2 — main parade route
Glow Market, Ward 7 — post-walk celebration hub
story_hooks: A geneware corporation has secretly funded a group of models with extreme modifications to walk at the front of Skinwalk Sunday, turning the organic event into an advertisement — the original Ward 2 community wants them removed without violence.
Someone has been documenting every Skinwalk Sunday participant with facial and biometric recognition and selling the data to employers — and the list includes Tier 4 workers who attended in disguise.
This year's Skinwalk Sunday route passes through a block that a corponation has quietly purchased and fenced — someone has to decide whether to reroute or walk through.
origin_event: A 2214 Ward 2 community decision to hold a single public walk where genetically modified residents could be visible without professional or social consequence, organized by local geneware artist Tomás Iyengar-Osei after a neighbor lost their Tier 2 employment contract for having visible chromatophore modification.
tier_observations: Tier 1 (Shelf): The purest expression — Ward 2 origin block is treated as sacred ground; extreme and experimental mods celebrated; handmade modification showcases; deeply communal. Tier 2: Large participation; the Calumet Mile route is a genuine street festival; some attend in partial modification, testing visibility. Tier 3: Growing attendance, often with more conservative mods; some attend as spectators; the event is becoming aspirational. Tier 4: Strictly private — some Tier 4 workers attend in disguise; official corporate policy discourages visible geneware modification in professional environments. Tier 5 (Spire): Completely absent from the event itself; several Spire residents fund research into 'elite geneware' but would never participate in the Walk.
